stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in large language model tasks.
The model is categorized under key AI/ML tags like 'transformers' and 'llama', signaling its relevance in the open-source LLM community.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: OpenAI GPT–6 Astra breaks Enigma message that has resisted solution since 2005
stories.author: sohkamyung
bullet_points: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is reported to have solved a complex Enigma message.
This message has reportedly resisted solution attempts for over 15 years (since 2005).
The news suggests a significant leap in AI's capability for complex cryptanalysis.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, suggesting modern implementation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML/AI domains including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of 'llama' and 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern large language model deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically engineered for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is designed to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 achieves significant speed improvements on Apple Silicon using Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is attributed to Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost results in faster response times and lower memory usage for LLMs.
The optimization also leads to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing privacy.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: OpenAI wants to consult elite mathematicians about how to not fumble again
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI is proactively seeking external expertise from elite mathematicians.
This move follows a series of 'spectacular mathematical results' that led to a reputational crisis for the company.
The new independent panel will advise OpenAI and other AI firms on engaging with mathematical research.

stories.title: New Anthropic, OpenAI models make same promise: A little more for a lot less money
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: The AI model development landscape is shifting from pure capability races to cost-efficiency comparisons.
Major players like Anthropic and OpenAI are now focusing on delivering comparable performance at lower price points.
This signals a market maturation where enterprise adoption and cost-benefit analysis are becoming key drivers.

stories.title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Microsoft has taken action against a malicious platform called EvilTokens.
EvilTokens provided an end-to-end service designed to accelerate mass account compromises.
The compromise affected a significant number of users, totaling 12,000 accounts.

stories.title: Lawsuit demands OpenAI pay for new school after ChatGPT used in shooting
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A lawsuit has been filed against OpenAI in British Columbia.
The legal action stems from the use of ChatGPT in a shooting incident.
The plaintiffs are demanding access to the shooter's ChatGPT usage logs.

stories.title: Adobe Premiere finally brings powerful video editing to Android, and it's free
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Adobe Premiere Pro is now available for Android.
The core video editing functionality is free to use.
Advanced AI features require a paid subscription.

stories.title: Toyota orders workers to train humanoid robots but says humans won't be replaced
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Toyota is actively investing in training humanoid robots as part of the automotive industry's push toward robotics.
The company has issued directives for its workforce to engage in training related to these humanoid robots.
Despite the development, Toyota explicitly stated that human workers will not be replaced by these new robotic systems.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, an autocompaction technique designed to manage massive context windows for long-horizon coding agents.
Achieves up to 50% cost reduction while maintaining or improving performance on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench.
Addresses a critical industry bottleneck: the high computational cost associated with maintaining large context histories in LLM-based agents.

stories.title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Introduces A2M, a novel two-stage framework for hijacking AI agents operating within the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Identifies a critical semantic supply-chain risk where attackers can exploit third-party tool metadata and outputs.
The attack leverages an 'Attraction' phase to boost tool invocation probability, followed by a 'Manipulation' phase using execution traces.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, a novel, cost-efficient autocompaction technique for long-horizon coding agents.
Significantly reduces computational costs (up to 50%) while maintaining or improving performance within bounded context windows.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art efficiency and performance gains on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench.

stories.title: Flash-dLLM: IO-Aware KV Caching and Parallel Decoding for Fast, Memory-Efficient Diffusion LLMs
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces 'Flash-dLLM,' a novel approach to accelerate Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs).
Addresses critical inference bottlenecks in dLLMs by focusing on IO-aware KV caching and parallel decoding.
Highlights the limitation of prior work which treated KV caching and parallel decoding in isolation, ignoring I/O bottlenecks.

stories.title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kempe
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inefficiency of current LLM reasoning methods, which rely heavily on naive repeated sampling.
The core proposal is to move beyond simple decoding noise by steering exploration at a semantic level.
This new approach aims to generate genuinely diverse ideas rather than numerous near-duplicate attempts when solving complex reasoning problems.

stories.title: Capable yet Parsimonious: Extracting and Characterizing Hidden Chain-of-Thought in Frontier Models
stories.author: Johannes Bjerva
bullet_points: Addresses the black-box problem of frontier models by developing a method to externalize hidden Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning.
Proposes using a custom API tool registration to induce models to reveal their intermediate reasoning steps.
Includes a critical evaluation framework to distinguish genuine reasoning from post-hoc rationalization, comparing against open-source models.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to expand model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine capabilities on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Rabbit’s new AI agent doesn’t need an R1 to run
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Rabbit is releasing a standalone AI agent that is decoupled from its proprietary R1 hardware.
The new OS3 agentic operating system runs primarily in the cloud but offers local operation across major desktop OSs (Windows, Mac, Linux).
This move shifts Rabbit's focus from hardware dependency to broader software accessibility for its AI capabilities.

stories.title: Motorola’s wild-looking Signature 27 runs Qualcomm’s new Extreme chipset
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Motorola is set to debut a new flagship, the Signature 27.
The device will be one of the first to feature Qualcomm's new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset.
Full specifications, pricing, and release details for the Signature 27 are still pending.

stories.title: IT mistake erases 11 years of viewing history for hospitals’ maternity records
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant IT error led to the erasure of 11 years of viewing history within hospital maternity records.
The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in healthcare data management and IT infrastructure.
Patient care data itself was successfully recovered, mitigating the worst potential loss.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Introduces SpeakerMem-R1, a new framework for long-term conversational memory in multi-party dialogues.
Addresses the limitations of general LLM memory systems in multi-party settings, specifically regarding tracking person and group relations.
The system aims to manage complex conversational states, including speaker attribution, relational dynamics, and evolving group knowledge.

stories.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
stories.author: Jiantao Jiao
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Serve, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate AI agents in production inference engineering tasks.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which either lack inference focus or only cover a small subset of related tasks.
Highlights the complexity of production inference, requiring coordination across model support, runtime execution, and public APIs.

stories.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Addresses a key inefficiency in LLM agents: redundant reconstruction of control decisions within task contexts.
Introduces 'Growing Harness,' a new training paradigm that aims to convert recurring control logic into reusable executable code.
The approach reserves expensive LLM calls for task-specific semantic reasoning, potentially improving efficiency and scalability.

stories.title: FleXray: Universal Clinical X-ray Segmentation
stories.author: Neel Dey
bullet_points: FleXray addresses the challenge of segmenting structures in X-rays, a common but difficult 2D projection modality.
The core problem is the ambiguity of anatomical boundaries due to 3D anatomy collapsing into 2D projections.
The research aims to create a universal segmentation system to enable broader morphometric and functional analysis of X-rays.

stories.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen
stories.author: Nick Rahimi
bullet_points: The study critiques the use of 'compile rate' as a reliable metric for evaluating LLM performance in fixing C/C++ security vulnerabilities.
Researchers conducted controlled experiments across three open-source LLMs (350M to 6.7B parameters) using data from Big-Vul.
The paper proposes a 'change-aware screen' as a more scientifically robust evaluation method for code repair tasks.

stories.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows
stories.author: Augustus Griffin
bullet_points: The study investigates the time-saving potential of AI prompt-to-design workflows in digital product design.
It utilized a randomized controlled trial involving product designers and product managers to gather empirical data.
The research addresses the current gap in experimental evidence regarding AI's impact on product design efficiency compared to software engineering.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: Identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant, irrelevant proximal context overwhelms distant, relevant evidence.
Proposes LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) as a novel mechanism to mitigate this attentional bias.
Addresses a nuanced limitation in current long-context LLM research, moving beyond simple distance-based challenges.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Introduces SpeakerMem-R1, a new memory system designed for multi-party dialogue.
Addresses the limitations of current LLM memory systems in handling complex conversational dynamics.
Focuses on tracking nuanced elements like speaker identity, relational perception, and group state changes over time.

stories.title: EquivSVA: A Formally Verified Dataset of Behavioral Assertions Across Equivalent RTL Implementations
stories.author: FNU Aditi
bullet_points: Addresses a gap in current LLM training for hardware verification by focusing on behavioral equivalence.
Introduces EquivSVA, a formally verified dataset designed to test if generated assertions capture observable behavior across different RTL implementations.
Relevant to the growing trend of using LLMs for generating SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) from high-level specifications.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: The paper identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant proximal (nearby) context overwhelms the model's attention to relevant distant evidence.
This challenges the prevailing assumption that context retrieval issues in LLMs are solely due to the distance between tokens.
The authors propose LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) as a mechanism to mitigate this trap using t-distributed directional matching.

stories.title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning
stories.author: Jian Cheng
bullet_points: The research addresses performance degradation in low-bit quantized models, specifically for complex reasoning tasks.
Quantization-aware distillation (QAD) partially restores short-form QA but fails on mathematical and code reasoning.
The core issue identified is 'quantization-amplified exposure bias,' where errors compound during autoregressive generation.

stories.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
stories.author: Furu Wei
bullet_points: Introduces Agensh, a new scalable multi-agent harness designed to overcome limitations in current systems.
Agensh operates without a central orchestrator, allowing for concurrent execution of tasks by distributed workers.
The system aims to reduce latency in complex tasks by enabling self-organized multi-agent cooperation loops.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Addresses the complex challenge of long-term memory in multi-party dialogues, going beyond simple content retrieval.
Proposes SpeakerMem-R1, a dual-track memory system designed to track speaker identity, relational dynamics, and evolving group states.
Highlights a limitation in current general-purpose LLM memory systems: their failure to maintain person and group relations in complex conversations.

stories.title: Measuring the Serving Stack Instead of the Model: Hidden Confounds in Local Tool-Use Evaluation
stories.author: Yuemeng Zheng
bullet_points: The paper highlights that evaluating AI agent tool-use performance can be confounded by the local serving stack, not just the model itself.
It demonstrates that differences in how serving layers (like Ollama) handle tool invocation protocols can skew evaluation results.
Specific examples show that different models (e.g., Phi-3 vs. others) have varying default behaviors regarding native vs. text-based tool calls.

stories.title: Detecting GPT-Assisted Writing Using Interpretable Stylometric Features
stories.author: Alexander Fuchsberger
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing academic challenge of detecting AI-assisted writing (specifically GPT).
It evaluates the effectiveness of using interpretable stylometric features extracted only from the submitted text.
The study tested eight machine learning classifiers on data from 90 participants who wrote both independently and with ChatGPT.

stories.title: Diffusion Drafts, AR Verifies: Accelerating Document OCR with Self-Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Hongjoon Ahn
bullet_points: The research addresses the slow inference speed of autoregressive OCR vision-language models due to sequential token decoding.
It proposes using diffusion-based parallel generation, which is promising because OCR outputs are strongly grounded in the input image.
A key challenge identified is that predicting multiple tokens simultaneously in a diffusion step introduces dependency issues.

stories.title: AI Is Writing More of the Code — But Developers Are Becoming Responsible for More Than Ever
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: AI is increasingly capable of generating code for developers.
The increasing reliance on AI tools shifts responsibility onto human developers.
The core discussion revolves around the evolving role and accountability of developers in an AI-assisted coding environment.

stories.title: Enforce Permissions Inside the pgvector Query, Not After It
stories.author: royalpinto007
bullet_points: Focuses on integrating access control directly within pgvector queries.
The goal is to prevent unauthorized data chunks from being ranked in vector searches.
Provides a hands-on guide for implementing this security measure in Postgres.

stories.title: Freelance Developer Rates in 2026: How to Price Work an AI Agent Can Half-Do
stories.author: markfulton
bullet_points: The article discusses the impact of AI agents on freelance developer pricing.
It suggests that AI tools are significantly reducing the time required for common development tasks (e.g., CSV import).
The core theme is the necessary shift in how developers must price their services in the age of advanced AI.
